chunks.why: Happy hermit-girl waters trees with friends; king arrives, admires her from hiding.
Playful teasing, jasmine-vine omen of marriage; bee scares her, king reveals himself courteously.
Learns she is nymph-born and marriageable; king gifts ring to remit her debt; brief elephant alarm.
Offstage; king smitten, invited to guard hermitage from demons: prospects for their union rising.
Bedridden with love-fever; writes lotus-leaf love letter; friends plot to unite her with king.
King answers her love, pledges her sole queenship; joy blooms, secret marriage effectively sealed.
Tender embrace interrupted; then Durvasas' curse falls: her lover will forget her unless he sees the ring.
Pregnant, adorned by heavenly gifts; Kanva blesses her; happy but bittersweet departure to husband.
Painful farewell to hermitage, fawn, and father; arrives at Dushyanta's court, still hopeful.
King fails to recognize her, publicly denies marriage; ring is lost; he insults her as cunning.
Hermits abandon her; she cries for a grave; heavenly light carries her off; fisherman finds the ring.
Offstage in nymph-care; king's memory restored, painting her portrait in remorse—her honour vindicated.
Offstage; king mourns picture and childlessness; Mishrakeshi observes; ring's story clears her name.
Offstage; king summoned by Indra to war; gods plan reunion; king still laments lost wife and heir.
Her son thrives in Kashyapa's grove; king meets the boy, amulet confirms paternity—recognition begins.
Full reunion; curse explained; Kashyapa blesses her, husband, and son Bharata; restored to queenship.
